speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger. To understand the cause, how long has this pain been developing?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury suggests a traumatic event, but the progressive nature of the swelling raises concern for infection or a specific inflammatory response. Did the finger turn red or warm to the touch immediately after the injury, or have those symptoms developed gradually since then?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The specific limitation at the distal interphalangeal joint and the extended resting position are classic signs of a specific tendon injury. Can you confirm if you were able to straighten your finger normally after the injury, or was the extension also affected?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (extensor tendon avulsion at the distal phalanx).

Based on the history of forced flexion injury, the inability to actively extend the fingertip, and the finger resting in a flexed position, this is consistent with a rupture of the extensor tendon. Given that you can straighten the finger when assisting it, the injury is likely an extensor tendon avulsion rather than a dislocation.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
